Result 111 found pFedMe handicapped by a fixed lambda of 15 that made its personalisation vacuous, and the fix -- sweeping lambda across separate runs and reporting the best -- overcorrected: choosing across runs is selection with hindsight, which neither competitor gets. This arm chooses inside each decision, on validation, and the outer scoring call is then frozen at that value so it cannot re-select on the test rows. It costs four full federated trainings per decision because lambda changes the whole trajectory rather than a final proximal solve. PREDICTIONS. (3) Adaptive shrinkage still leads on mean share across the eight above-floor pools. WITHDRAWAL: if pfedme_cv beats adaptive shrinkage on mean share above the floor, then section 6's recommendation loses to a published personalisation method under a fully symmetric comparison, and the paper must say so and reframe around the downside column alone.
